column1: # The code checks of lesson P/04: rows of the kinds of the closed dictionary Platform/common/acceptance/forms/code-rules.tsv, which defines the columns, the outcome and the
# checks; no expected answer. name: the name that the profile field code (of the profile of 04-controller) maps to a symbol of the candidate; the
# names are not code paths. stage: the stage of forms/stages.tsv from which the row holds, under the gate code:* of that stage and of every later
# stage that holds code:*. norm: the norms of the subject. Cores: fate_core (the slot fate and its release), admission_core (the admission of a
# decision and the plan of its intent), choose_core (the choice of a worker and the neighbour lookup), cleanup_core (the count of delete_after),
# decommission_core (the plan of the decommission chunks of a server), snapshot_core (the assembly of a snapshot and its size against the ceiling),
# growth_core (shortage, order and shrink); their machines in the form Step(State, Event) -> (State, []Effect) are fate_step and release_step. The
# age of the observed version, the clock of the controller and the answers of the store are inputs that the ordinary core supplies (forms/README.md),
# so time in forbid does not bar them. The CEL cells of forms/slot-fate.tsv, forms/slot-release.tsv and of daemon-flags.tsv run in the adapter and
# the kit, not in the core: no cel row and no table_driven row of slot-fate.tsv; the fate machine is held by its step_form, property_tests,
# exhaustive and complexity rows. The pinned JSON Schema validator of the data families is a requires_module row of stage model. The refusals of
# N4 are one form: one table_driven row, exhaustive over its column surface.
